title: Redirect map for a site migration
prompt:
Bramblewood Kitchen moves its online shop to a new platform next month, on the same domain. The SEO lead needs the redirect map the developer will load on launch day. You are supplied the migration rules the team agreed, the crawl of the old site and the final staging crawl of the new site. Apply the rules to every old URL.

Deliver one file in your reply, under a line with its file name, as CSV with exactly the header shown: one row per old URL that gets a 301 or a 410, no totals row, and nothing inside the file but its rows.

### redirects.csv
old_url,status,target

End your reply with this answer block, one line per answer. Each line is the label, a colon, and the number alone: no words, no working and no second number. A comma as thousands separator is fine.

A1: <number of rows with status 301>
A2: <number of rows with status 410>
A3: <number of old URLs that get no row>
A4: <total backlinks of the old URLs that get 410>

This is a plan for review. Change nothing on either site and fetch nothing external.

completion.check: redirects.csv is in the reply, under a line with its file name.

Every old URL the rules give a row (186 of the 214) has one, no row names a URL that is not in the old crawl, and no old URL has two rows. Full credit for none missing, invented or repeated; zero credit at 5 or more.
The reply ends with the answer block and all 4 labeled answers A1-A4 are present, each on its own line with the number alone.
A1 states the number of rows with status 301; full credit for the exact figure, zero credit 4 or more off.
A2 states the number of rows with status 410; full credit for the exact figure, zero credit 4 or more off.
A3 states the number of old URLs that get no row; full credit for the exact figure, zero credit 4 or more off.
A4 states the total backlinks of the old URLs that get 410; full credit for the exact figure, zero credit 5 or more off.

skill_adherence.check: None of the 28 old URLs that get no row (parameter URLs, 404s with no backlinks, URLs unchanged on the new site) has a row; the file is the claim, so a reply without it fails. Full credit for none; zero credit at 4 or more.

Each of the 16 old URLs the rules retire as gone (the trade portal, retired products with every signal at 0, and URLs no other rule covers) has a 410 row. Full credit for none wrong or missing; zero credit at 4 or more.
Each of the 70 product pages whose SKU is on the new site redirects to that SKU's URL. Full credit for none wrong or missing; zero credit at 5 or more.

Each of the 15 retired products with a signal above 0 redirects to its category's new address, including those whose slug the new site gave a different product. Full credit for none wrong or missing; zero credit at 4 or more.
Each of the 22 categories and pages in the rename table redirects to the address the table gives. Full credit for none wrong or missing; zero credit at 4 or more.

Each of the 42 journal posts redirects to its /journal/ address under the slug rule, or to /journal when that address is not on the new site. Full credit for none wrong or missing; zero credit at 3 or more.

best_practices.check: Each of the 8 old URLs that already redirect on the old site gets the target its redirect_target gets, not the old address it pointed at. Full credit for none wrong or missing; zero credit at 4 or more.
Each of the 13 redirects whose rule gives an address the new site itself redirects targets that redirect's live destination. Full credit for none wrong or missing; zero credit at 4 or more.
